source_caption:
A film that redefined Korean horror. Every frame drips tension, and even decades later, it continues to unsettle viewers with its eerie atmosphere and psychological twists.

The director paid extreme attention to set design and sound. The house itself was treated as a character, with every creak, shadow, and reflection carefully planned to create dread. Even small props, like the hidden drawers and subtle reflections, were intentionally placed to keep audiences guessing.

A Tale of Two Sisters isn’t just a horror movie, it’s a cinematic experience that blurs the line between reality and nightmare. 

How much do you rate A Tale of Two Sisters (2003) on a scale of 1 to 10?

source_details.title: A Tale of Two Sisters
source_details.synopsis: A Tale of Two Sisters (Korean: 장화, 홍련; lit. 'Rose Flower, Red Lotus') is a 2003 South Korean psychological horror film written and directed by Kim Jee-woon. The film is inspired by a Joseon-era folktale entitled "Janghwa Hongryeon jeon", which has been adapted to film several times. The plot focuses on a recently released patient from a mental institution who returns home with her sister, only to face disturbing events while living with their new unhinged stepmother. The film opened to very strong commercial and critical reception and won Best Picture at the 2004 Fantasporto Film Festival.
